title: Officer Shoots Suspect After Being Struck With Machete
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Susanville, California — On Wednesday, May 6, 2026, at about 12:25 a.m., two Susanville Police officers were dispatched after receiving information that Ngirasiau "Derek" Sikong was behaving erratically, possibly under the influence of methamphetamine, and had threatened children while armed with a machete. When officers arrived, Sikong allegedly became increasingly agitated and, during a tense standoff from an upstairs window, held a two-year-old child outside before pulling the child back inside and making movements that led officers to believe the child faced an immediate risk of serious harm. The situation escalated rapidly when Officer David Lee fired through a second-story window after observing what appeared to be a downward strike with the machete toward the child. As officers entered the residence moments later, investigators said Sikong charged toward them with the machete and wounded Officer Lee, causing a severe shoulder injury. Officer Lee then returned fire, while Officer KC Capron deployed a less-lethal round after Sikong continued to ignore commands. Three children inside the home were located unharmed, but Sikong later died from gunshot wounds despite officers' efforts to provide emergency medical care. Officer Lee was treated at a hospital and released. After reviewing body-camera footage, witness statements, and forensic interviews, prosecutors determined that both officers' use of force was justified and announced that no criminal charges will be filed.
